metrics.title: Resource Graph Metrics

sections.basic_desc: Fundamental metrics about the graph structure. Helps understand the overall complexity of the resource system.
sections.centrality_desc: Identifies the most important and connected resources in the system. Central resources can be bottlenecks or strategic points.
sections.connectivity_desc: Analyzes how resources are interconnected. Disconnected components may indicate isolated mechanics.
sections.node_stats_desc: Distribution of element types in the game. Helps balance the number of resources vs cards.
sections.edge_stats_desc: Balance between production and consumption of resources. Large differences may indicate imbalance.
sections.production_desc: Identifies the most produced and consumed resources. Resources with high demand and low production can be problems.
sections.path_desc: Shows how resources are connected and dependent on each other. Long paths may indicate complex chains, cycles may create infinite loops.

tooltips.nodes: Total resources and cards in the game
tooltips.edges: Total number of relations between cards and resources
tooltips.density: Ratio of existing vs possible connections. High values indicate a complex system.
tooltips.multigraph: Allows multiple connections between the same nodes
tooltips.average_degree: Average connections per node. Indicates the average level of interconnection.
tooltips.diameter: Longest distance between two nodes. Shows the longest dependency chain.
tooltips.average_eccentricity: Average distance between nodes. High values indicate long paths between resources.
tooltips.connected: Whether all nodes are connected directly or indirectly
tooltips.connected_components: Number of isolated subgraphs. Ideally should be 1 for a cohesive system.
tooltips.resources: Total number of different resources in the game
tooltips.total_resources: Sum of all available resource quantities
tooltips.cards: Total number of cards that interact with resources
tooltips.gains: Total number of resource productions and total quantity produced
tooltips.costs: Total number of resource consumptions and total quantity consumed

path.most_demanded_hint: This resource is consumed by many cards but has few production sources, and could become a bottleneck.
path.cycles_hint: Cycles can create infinite loops or powerful combos. Check if they are intentional.

overview.title: Welcome to the Balancing Tool
overview.intro_1: This is an application for designers and developers who want to analyze and balance resource-based card games. The tool lets you load a JSON model containing cards, resources, and rules, then simulate matches, view network metrics, and explore all reachable states of the system.
overview.intro_2: The goal is to identify bottlenecks, underutilized resources, long production chains, and imbalances right at the start of design, saving time and improving the player experience.
overview.interface_top: Top: Available resources (action, wood, plank, score, etc.) and the current seed.
overview.interface_controls: Control Bar: Buttons for game actions, toggling the analysis panel, persistence, and theme.
overview.interface_game_area: Game Area: Cards in hand, offer (market), and resources.
overview.interface_analysis: Analysis Panel: Tabs for Graph, Petri Net, Reachability Tree, and History.
overview.tip: Tip: Use the "Show Analyses" button to open the panel and explore the diagnostic tools.

gameplay.title: Example Gameplay
gameplay.intro: The tool includes an example game with fixed rules (available in data/cards.ts) to demonstrate how it works. You can interact with it to understand how resources flow and how the analyses reflect the game state.
gameplay.resource_acao: Action: Main resource – every card costs 1 action to be played or bought.
gameplay.resource_madeira_pedra: Raw Wood and Raw Stone: Basic resources collected.
gameplay.resource_tabua: Plank and Polished Stone: Resources processed from the basic ones.
gameplay.resource_pontuacao: Score: Victory resource – whoever scores the most wins.
gameplay.turns_p1: Each turn starts with 3 actions. Playing a card or buying from the offer costs 1 action.
gameplay.turns_p2: The "Pass Turn" button ends the turn, refills 3 actions, and draws new cards from the deck. The "Decrease Action" and "Increase Point" buttons are debug tools for testing.
gameplay.note: Note: This is just an example game. The real power of the tool lies in the analyses and the ability to load your own models.

victory.title: Victory System and Deadlocks
victory.intro: The simulation can end in three ways, all configurable in the JSON model:
victory.points_p: When a player reaches or exceeds pontosParaVencer (default: 10).
victory.turns_p: When the number of turns exceeds turnosMaximos (default: 30).
victory.deadlock_p: Occurs when the player has no actions left and cannot play or buy any card. The tool distinguishes:
victory.deadlock_temp: Temporary Deadlock: The player is out of actions but can buy cards that generate action (e.g., "Rest") – YELLOW alert in the Petri Net.
victory.deadlock_perm: Permanent Deadlock: There is no card that produces action anywhere – RED alert. The game cannot continue.
victory.note: Example: with pontosParaVencer: 15, 15 points are needed to win. Adjust these values in the JSON to test different scenarios.

graph.title: Graph Analysis
graph.intro: The Resource Graph visually displays the relationships between cards and resources. It is a fundamental tool for identifying bottlenecks and imbalances.
graph.metric_density: Density: Ratio of existing vs. possible connections. High density indicates a complex, interconnected system.
graph.metric_centrality: Centrality: Identifies the most important resources (heavily used as input/output).
graph.metric_diameter: Diameter: Longest distance between two nodes. High values suggest very long production chains.
graph.metric_components: Components: Disconnected subgraphs. Ideally should be 1 (all resources are connected).
graph.metric_production: Production vs. Consumption: If production > consumption, resources tend to accumulate; if consumption > production, there is a risk of shortage.
graph.balance_gargalos: Bottlenecks: heavily consumed but rarely produced resources.
graph.success: Use the graph to quickly detect resources with high demand and low supply.

petri.title: Petri Net
petri.intro: The Petri Net is a mathematical model for concurrent systems. In this tool, it shows the interaction between resources (places) and cards (transitions) in real time.
petri.elem_places: Places (Green Circles): Resources. The number inside is the current quantity (tokens).
petri.elem_transitions: Transitions (Blue Rectangles): Cards. They turn yellow when enabled.
petri.feat_free_mode: Free Mode: Allows manually editing tokens by clicking on places (left +1, right -1). Useful for testing hypothetical scenarios.
petri.feat_full_analysis: Full Analysis: Ignores the player's hand and shows all possible transitions of the system – global view.
petri.feat_slider: Expansions Slider: Controls how many extra steps the reachability tree will explore from ω (omega) states.
petri.feat_generate: Generate Tree: Builds the reachability tree from the current marking.
petri.how_to_p1: Enable the "Free Mode" switch. Click with the left button on a resource to add 1 token, with the right to remove.
petri.how_to_p2: To fire a transition (card), click on it. If it is enabled (yellow), resources will be consumed and produced according to the rule.
petri.info: <yellow>Yellow</yellow> transitions are enabled – you have enough resources to fire them.

reachability.title: Reachability Tree
reachability.intro: The Reachability Tree enumerates all possible states of the system from the current marking. It is a powerful tool to check whether the game can enter loops, whether there are dead states, or whether resources can grow infinitely (omega).
reachability.feat_auto: Automatic Expansion: The tree is generated recursively from the initial marking, firing all enabled transitions.
reachability.feat_omega: Omega (ω) Detection: Identifies resources that can grow indefinitely – represented as ω.
reachability.feat_control: Expansion Control: The expansions slider defines how many extra layers the tree will explore beyond ω states (useful to avoid combinatorial explosion).
reachability.feat_visualization: Hierarchical Visualization: Navigate through states by clicking on the tree nodes.
reachability.feat_table: Detailed Table: Lists all generated states with:
reachability.bullet_transition: • Transition that led to the state
reachability.bullet_type: • Type: initial, ω, cyclic, terminal, simulation
reachability.bullet_button: • Button to center the node in the visualization
reachability.how_to_1: 1. Adjust the expansions slider (0-10) to control the depth.
reachability.how_to_2: 2. Click "Generate Tree" – the tree will be built from the current marking (or from the game's marking, if "Full Analysis" is active).
reachability.how_to_3: 3. Explore the states in the interactive visualization or in the table below.
reachability.success: The tree reveals whether the system can enter infinite loops or whether there are unwanted terminal states – essential for validating balance.

custom_models.title: Custom JSON Models
custom_models.intro: You can create your own games by loading a JSON file. This is the most powerful way to use the tool – define cards, resources, rules, and simulate as many times as you want.
custom_models.load_p1: 1. Click the "Persistence" button in the control bar.
custom_models.load_p2: 2. Select "Load rules (JSON)" in the dropdown menu.
custom_models.load_p3: 3. Navigate to the .json file and select it.
custom_models.load_p4: 4. The game will automatically restart with your custom rules!
custom_models.success: Tip: Use "Save to File" in the persistence menu to export your current game and edit it as a model.
